title: Smooth prime-to-characteristic curve calculation
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and let $C$ be a smooth curve over $k$ [def-sc-curves], that is, a smooth separated finite-type $k$-scheme with $\dim C\leq1$, possibly empty or disconnected. Let $\ell$ be a prime different from $\operatorname{char}k$, and let $F=\underline{\mathbf F_\ell}=\underline{\mathbf Z/\ell\mathbf Z}$ be the constant abelian etale sheaf [def-sc-constant-sheaves]. Then all eight applicable assertions $\mathcal C_j(C,F)$, $1\leq j\leq8$, of [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions] hold. The field-extension maps are the canonical pullback maps of [def-sc-field-extension], and the open-restriction maps are those of [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback], induced by pulling back etale cocycles.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ (a field is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0$ and $k$), and then [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finite-components]. Thus $C$ has finitely many irreducible components. Group these components by the equivalence relation generated by nonempty intersection. Within each group their union is connected: irreducible spaces are connected, and adding a member intersecting the previous union preserves connectedness. Distinct groups have disjoint unions. Each union and its complement are finite unions of closed components, hence each union is clopen. They are exactly the connected components, since a connected subset cannot meet two members of a clopen partition. Let these nonempty clopen schemes be $C_i$, indexed by a finite set $I$; for empty $C$, take $I=\varnothing$. The restrictions of the structure map are smooth and separated, with finite type and dimension at most one: restrict smooth charts and the diagonal to the open, use quasi-compactness of a clopen subset to restrict a finite affine cover, and view chains of specializations in the open as chains in $C$.

proof.text: For each zero-dimensional $C_i$, [lem-sc-zero-dim-noetherian-finite-discrete] makes its space finite discrete, and connectedness makes it a singleton. An affine neighbourhood of that point is the whole scheme, say $C_i=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Its local ring equals $A$ since it has only one prime, its maximal ideal. By [lem-sc-smooth-regular] this ring is a domain; its zero ideal is therefore its unique prime, so its maximal ideal is zero and $A$ is a field. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base] the structure map $k\to A$ is an isomorphism. Thus $C_i\simeq\operatorname{Spec}k$ as a $k$-scheme. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-zero-dimensional-cohomology] and [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-geometric-stalk]: $H^0(C_i,F)=\mathbf Z/\ell\mathbf Z$ canonically, and $H^q(C_i,F)=0$ for $q>0$. The constant sheaf is locally constant with finite stalks on the single stratum $C_i$, hence constructible; its stalks are killed by $\ell$, so are prime to the characteristic. This gives C1--C5 (C3 whenever its hypothesis holds) and C8, since any open is empty or the point. After extension $k'/k$, the component is $\operatorname{Spec}k'$. Again higher cohomology is zero. In degree zero [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] identifies the germ of a pulled-back section with the original germ, so the map is the identity on $\mathbf Z/\ell\mathbf Z$. It is an isomorphism, giving C6 and C7 with the actual pullback maps.

source.place: Lemma 0A5B (lemma-constant-smooth-statements), proof, Case I and component reduction

proof.text: For a one-dimensional $C_i$ the hypotheses of the connected calculations hold exactly. Apply [lem-sc-c1] with $n=\ell$ for C1, and [lem-sc-c2] when $C_i$ is affine for C2. The constant $\mathbf Z/\ell\mathbf Z$ sheaf is constructible: the one-stratum partition and its identity etale covering exhibit local constancy, and its stalks are the finite group $\mathbf Z/\ell\mathbf Z$ by [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-geometric-stalk] and the definition [def-weil-pbc-constructible-torsion]. Every stalk element is killed by $\ell$, hence has order prime to positive $\operatorname{char}k$; in characteristic zero there is no additional condition [def-weil-pbc-primary-torsion]. Apply [lem-sc-c4] for C4 and, when $C_i$ is proper, [lem-sc-c5] for C5.

source.place: Lemma 0A5B (lemma-constant-smooth-statements), proof, Case I and component reduction

proof.text: For C3 on a nonempty one-dimensional component, characteristic zero has no C3 hypothesis. In characteristic $p>0$, we have $p\ne\ell$. Choose any geometric point. Under [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-geometric-stalk] the element $1\in\mathbf Z/\ell\mathbf Z$ is nonzero and no power of $p$ kills it: $\ell$ cannot divide $p^a$. Consequently the constant sheaf is not $p$-primary in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-primary-torsion]. The conditional assertion C3 therefore holds vacuously. This is the coprime-primary case, not an invocation of the equal-characteristic Artin--Schreier theorem.

source.place: Lemma 0A5B (lemma-constant-smooth-statements), proof, Case I and component reduction

proof.text: On every one-dimensional component apply [lem-sc-c6] with $r=\ell$ for C6 and [lem-sc-c7] when that component is proper for C7. Their statements explicitly assert that the pullback maps $\rho^q_{k'/k}$ are isomorphisms, so no identification with a noncanonical abstract group isomorphism is used. Apply [lem-sc-c8] with $r=\ell$ for C8; it asserts surjectivity of the actual restriction map for every open immersion, including empty and whole opens.

source.place: Lemma 0A5B (lemma-constant-smooth-statements), proof, Case I and component reduction

proof.text: Every $C_i$ now satisfies the eight assertions. Use [lem-pbc-k2-clopen-constant-assertions] with coefficient ring $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$, module $M=\mathbf Z/\ell\mathbf Z$, and the finite pairwise disjoint clopen covering from step 1. It gives the eight assertions on $C$ itself, including the empty covering case. In particular it gives the C6, C7 and C8 maps appearing in their definitions, not newly chosen isomorphisms. By [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] these maps send a cocycle to its image under the inverse-image unit and the comparison of resolutions; the field-extension instances are exactly [def-sc-field-extension]. Thus their prescribed map is the pullback of etale cocycles, as claimed.
